Q: 403 Client Error while using Partner Center API A:

Alright, the issue is that Partner Center has its own permission system, separate from Azure AD. Even if your app has the right API permissions in Azure, you also need to assign a role to your app directly in Set up API access in Partner Center

Once that is done, update your getClients function to include the MS-PartnerCenter-Application-Name

def getClients(token):
    url = "https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers"
    headers = {
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
        "Accept": "application/json",
        "MS-PartnerCenter-Application-Name": "your-app-name"#i mean ts one in the header
    }
    r = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()

Once the role is assigned, your token will carry the right claims and the 403 should go away. let me know if it works.

Q: Integer Partition Regex A:

I understand that I shouldn't use regexes for this, but I can't blame you for not knowing that.

The code isn't even correct, here's a better way:

def calc(ref: int, s: str) -> bool:
    return bool(re.fullmatch(r"(\+\d*)*", s)) and sum(map(int, s.split("+")[1:])) == ref

Your code didn't check if it was even a sum of numbers. Also, this code would be essentially the equivalent of bool(re.fullmatch(partition_regex, s)). What if I wanted to do a re.search?

Q: How do I define a C/C++ preprocessor variable in Meson? A:

You can pass a macro definition to the compiler command line arguments via the meson c_args argument, like this:

my_defs = []

if some_condition
    my_defs += '-DMY_MESON_VARIABLE'
endif

executable('myexecutable',
    'src/main.c',
    'src/etc.c',
    # more arguments

    c_args: my_defs,
)

This might look non-portable at a first glance, but according to the meson manual it isn't, since all compiler actually implement the -D option in the same way.

Alternatively, you can use Meson's configure_file() function to generate a header of project specific macro definitions and include that where needed, instead of passing the macros on the command line.

Example:

conf = configuration_data()
conf.set10('MY_MESON_VARIABLE', some_bool_condition);

configure_file(output : 'config.h', configuration : conf)
